src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies

s: The Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC) is a key part of
src: APPSC Group-II Services Main Examination (Notification 25/2018), Paper III: Planning in India and Indian Economy; Contemporary Problems and Developments, held 30-08-2019 (Shift 2) · Q68
x: VCIC is part of the East Coast Economic Corridor, with ADB support and links to the Golden Quadrilateral, so all the listed options apply.

s: As per the Act, the duration of special status to Andhra Pradesh will be for
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
x:
Most keys: five years 'as per the Act'. Strictly: SCS is not in the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014; the five years come from the PM's Rajya Sabha assurance of 20 Feb 2014.
Five years – the period PM Manmohan Singh promised in the Rajya Sabha on 20 February 2014. The Act itself contains no SCS clause.

s: The 'NGTS-4b' known as the forbidden planet was discovered recently from the atmosphere of which Planet?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: NGTS-4b, the 'forbidden planet' (2019), is a Neptune-sized exoplanet found in the 'Neptunian desert' near its star; so the intended answer is Neptune (the question's 'from the atmosphere of' is garbled wording).

s: Which among the following is not a unit of distance?
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Light year, parsec and astronomical unit are units of distance; 'longsec' is not a unit of distance at all, so it is the answer (the original options are not in the scan).

s: From the choices below, the best estimate of the age of the Universe is --------- years old.
src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
x: The age of the universe is about 13.8 billion years; the Earth and solar system are about 4.6 billion years old.

s: What is the distance from the Sun to Earth measured in astronomical unit/s?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: The astronomical unit is defined as the mean Sun–Earth distance, so that distance is 1 AU (about 149.6 million km).

s: Which Spacecraft is the first to land on the far side of the moon?
src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
x: China's Chang'e 4 made the first soft landing on the far side of the Moon on 3 January 2019 (Von Kármán crater), with the Yutu-2 rover.

s: Google and NASA have joined hands to identify which two new planets around distant stars?
src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
x: In December 2017 Google's machine learning on NASA Kepler data found Kepler-90i (giving Kepler-90 eight planets, like our solar system) and Kepler-80g.

s: Which of the following planets has the highest number of natural satellites?
src: APPSC Group-II Services Main Examination (Notification 25/2018), Paper I: General Studies and Mental Ability, held 29-08-2019 (Shift 1; Mental Ability questions omitted) · Q91
x: In 2019 Jupiter had the most known moons (79); Saturn overtook it later.

s: A level surface is a surface ____ to the ____ of the earth
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: In surveying, a level surface is a curved surface parallel to the mean spheroidal surface of the earth (every point normal to the plumb line). Off-topic (geodesy/surveying), moved to Earth – shape and geoid.

s: Earth Day is celebrated every year on
src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
x: Earth Day is observed every year on 22 April; it was first observed in 1970.

s: The area represented by contours whose values decrease towards the centre (1300, 1280, 1260 from outer to inner) is a ____
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Closed contours whose values fall towards the centre show a depression (hollow); rising values would show a hill. Off-topic (maps/contours), moved.

s: Which of the following has the maximum velocity of rotation?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: The linear speed of rotation is maximum at the Equator (about 1,670 km/h) and zero at the poles.

s: What would be the local time off the coast of West Africa in longitude 10° W if it was 3.40pm GMT in London?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: 10° west of Greenwich is 10 × 4 = 40 minutes behind, so 3:40 p.m. GMT is 3:00 p.m. at 10°W.

s: Which of the following Indian States is not bisected by the Tropic of Cancer ?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q3
x: The Tropic of Cancer passes through eight States (Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram); Odisha lies wholly south of it.

s: Which river of India passes the Tropic of Cancer twice?
src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test (2018 recruitment), held 28-05-2019 · Q43
x: The Mahi rises in MP, loops through Rajasthan and crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice.

s:
Vernal equinox occurs: a. March 20 or 21 b. September 22 or 23 c. March 22 or 23 d. September 20 or 21
Choose the correct option from the codes given below.
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: The vernal (spring) equinox is 20/21 March in the Northern Hemisphere and 22/23 September in the Southern Hemisphere, so both a and b. Dates c and d are not equinoxes.

s: Isogonic lines pass through points of ____
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Isogonic lines join points of equal magnetic declination; isoclinic lines join points of equal dip.

s: Basalt is an
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: Basalt forms when lava cools fast on the surface – a fine-grained extrusive igneous rock.

s: Find the correct statement/s: 1. Igneous rocks have no layers. 2. Limestone is white as well as black 3. Fossils are found in the igneous rocks
src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
x: Igneous rocks have no layers and limestone occurs white as well as black (1, 2 true); fossils are not found in igneous rocks (3 false).

s: Which one of the followings is an example of Metamorphic rocks
src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
x: Marble (from limestone) is a metamorphic rock.

s: Petrology is
src: APPSC Group-II Paper-I General Studies & Mental Ability 2019
x: Petrology is the study (science) of rocks, a part of geology.

s: Petrology is
src: APPSC Group-II Services Main Examination (Notification 25/2018), Paper I: General Studies and Mental Ability, held 29-08-2019 (Shift 1; Mental Ability questions omitted) · Q84
x: Petrology is the branch of geology that studies rocks.

s: The age, density, and thickness of oceanic crust ____ with distance from the mid-ocean ridge.
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Away from the mid-ocean ridge the age, density and thickness of oceanic crust (and sediment) increase.

s: Most geologists classify a mountain as a landform that rises at least ____ above its surrounding area.
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Most geologists treat a landform as a mountain if it rises at least about 300 m (1,000 ft) above the surrounding area.

s: Aravalli ranges are an example of
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: The Aravallis are one of the oldest fold mountain systems in the world (old fold, now residual).

s: The tallest mountain measured from top to bottom is ____ which stands tall for more than 10000 meters
answer: Mauna Kea, an inactive volcano on island of Hawaii
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Measured from its base on the Pacific floor, Mauna Kea (a dormant shield volcano on Hawaii, 4,207 m above sea level) is over 10,000 m tall – taller than Everest base-to-peak. PMF gives ~9,140 m from the ocean floor; USGS/NOAA put base-to-peak at ~10,210 m.

s: Solidification of molten material magma leads to formation of
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: Igneous rocks form from the cooling and solidification of magma or lava.

s: A dormant volcano
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening Test 2019 (Notification 07/2019, booklet OBF/444), held 16-06-2019 · Q21
x: A dormant volcano has not erupted for a long time but is not extinct and can erupt again.

s: Andhra Pradesh comes under which earthquake classified zone?
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: Andhra Pradesh lies in Seismic Zones II and III; it has no Zone IV or V area.

s: The point, on the earth's surface, directly above the point where an earthquake occurs, is termed the
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: The epicentre is the point on the surface directly above the focus where the earthquake originates.

s: A geophysicist who studies earthquakes and the mechanical characteristics of the Earth is called ______.
src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
x: A scientist who studies earthquakes and the mechanical behaviour of the Earth is a seismologist; the science is seismology.

s: Geologists who specifically study earthquakes are called
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Scientists who study earthquakes are seismologists.

s: Which of the following is not part of geological disaster?
src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
x: A sea (storm) surge is a hydro-meteorological hazard driven by cyclonic winds and low pressure; earthquakes, landslides, tsunamis and volcanic eruptions are the geological disasters.

s: India has been divided into how many Seismic Risk Zones?
src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test (2018 recruitment), held 28-05-2019 · Q51
x: The Bureau of Indian Standards divides India into four seismic zones, II to V.

s: Equal percentage of sand, clay and silt forms
src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
x: A soil with roughly balanced proportions of sand, silt and clay is loam (loamy soil).

s: The movement of earthy materials from higher region to lower region due to gravitational pull is called
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: The downslope movement of earth material under gravity is mass movement; its sudden form is a landslide. Off-topic (mass wasting), moved.

s: The largest delta of Indian Subcontinent is
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: The Ganga-Brahmaputra (Sundarbans) delta is the largest delta of the subcontinent and of the world.

s: In which one of the following streams, there is no apparent reason why it follows the path it takes
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: An insequent stream shows no apparent control by slope or structure, so there is no clear reason for its course; it typically forms a dendritic pattern on uniform rock.

s: In which type of drainage pattern the mainstream bends at right angles and the tributaries join at right angles.
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: In rectangular drainage, controlled by joints and faults, the main stream bends at right angles and tributaries join it at right angles.

s: Drainage Pattern of River Krishna is
src: APPSC Executive Officer Grade-III in A.P. Endowments Sub-Service Screening Test (Notification 24/2021), Section A (General Studies), held 24-07-2022 · Q33
x: The Krishna follows the original eastward slope of the Deccan plateau, so it is a consequent river.

s: Which layer of atmosphere contains the ozone layer?
src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
x: The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere (mainly 15–35 km), where it absorbs UV radiation.

s: Which of the following the second layer of atmosphere:
src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspectors, Agriculture Office
x: Above the troposphere lies the stratosphere (to 50 km), the second layer, with the ozone layer.

s: What is the thin layer of gases around the earth called?
src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Computer Assistant in ANGRAU Gene
x: The atmosphere is the thin layer (envelope) of gases surrounding the Earth, held by gravity.

s: The region between ~ 30° to 35° north and 30° to 35° south latitudes is characterized by weak winds. This region is called
src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
x: The calm subtropical high-pressure belt at about 30–35° N and S is called the horse latitudes.

s: Anemometer is an instrument used to measure.
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: An anemometer measures wind speed; a wind vane shows direction.

s: Which liquid is used in an aneroid barometer?
answer: No liquid – an aneroid barometer has no liquid (it uses a partly evacuated metal box)
src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
x: 'Aneroid' means 'without liquid': the barometer works by an evacuated metal capsule that expands and contracts with pressure; a mercury barometer uses mercury. No printed answer.

s: Low pressure area is called
src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
x: A low-pressure area with winds converging and spiralling inward is a cyclone (depression); a high-pressure area is an anticyclone.

s: Which cloud type produces rainstorms?
src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
x: Cumulonimbus clouds, tall and dense, bring thunderstorms and heavy rain.

s: Line joining places having equal degree of cloudiness is known as
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Lines joining places with equal cloudiness are isonephs.

s: Falling water droplets of less than 0.5 mm diameter:
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Drizzle is light precipitation of drops smaller than 0.5 mm; rain drops are larger than 0.5 mm.

s: Which chemical salt is used in cloud seeding?
src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
x: Silver iodide is the main cloud-seeding salt – its crystal structure mimics ice.

s: Rate of transpiration is reduced by
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: Low light closes the stomata, so transpiration falls; high humidity, low temperature and still air also reduce it.

s: When the air temperature and dew point are equal the relative humidity is:
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: When air cools to its dew point it is saturated, so air temperature = dew point means relative humidity is 100%.

s:

b. Air - 2. Hydro
c. Water - 3. Bio

x: Litho means stone, atmo vapour/air, hydro water and bio life, giving lithosphere, atmosphere, hydrosphere and biosphere.

s: Which of the following public figures picked up a broom to help clean the cyclone-hit port city of Visakhapatnam?
answer: M. Venkaiah Naidu (Union Urban Development Minister, Oct 2014)
src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
x: Union Urban Development Minister M. Venkaiah Naidu wielded a broom on a Visakhapatnam beach on 24 Oct 2014 (Swachh Bharat) to clear Hudhud debris; no report found of Anushka Sharma taking part.

s: Tundra is usually a wet place because
answer: the low temperatures cause evaporation of water to be slow
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: The tundra stays wet because the low temperatures keep evaporation slow, and the permafrost below stops melt-water draining away.

s: A scrub forest found in California, along the Mediterranean Sea, and along the southern coast of Australia, where the annual rainfall ranges from 65 cm to 75 cm and the majority of the rain falls in the winter falls in ____ Biome
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Chaparral is the Mediterranean scrub biome of California, the Mediterranean coast and southern Australia, with mostly winter rain.

s: An example of climatic control:
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Altitude is a control (factor) of climate: temperature falls about 6.5°C per 1,000 m, so Shimla is cooler than Amritsar.

s: Select the sequence in increasing order of percent of total volume of marine sediments:
answer: Deep-ocean floor, Continental shelves, Continental rises, Continental slopes
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Marine sediments are concentrated on the continental margins (about 90% of the volume on about a quarter of the floor), so the deep-ocean floor holds the least. The relative shares of shelf, rise and slope were not found in the library or on the web; the printed order of those three is kept but unve

s: Which of the following is the smallest Ocean?
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: The Arctic is the smallest of the five oceans.

s: The largest part of our hydrosphere is:
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, about a third of the Earth's surface, so it is the largest part of the hydrosphere.

s: Select the correct sequence of the seas arranged in ascending order of salinity
answer: Baltic Sea, Black Sea, Red Sea, Dead Sea
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Ascending salinity: Baltic (under 10‰) < Black Sea (17–18‰) < Red Sea (~41‰) < Dead Sea (~238‰).

s: Which year was declared as International year of fresh water?
src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
x: The UN General Assembly declared 2003 the International Year of Freshwater.

s: Blue colour of sea water is due to
answer: Scattering of sunlight by water molecules (with absorption of red light) – not interference
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: Sea water looks blue because water absorbs red light and its molecules scatter blue light (C.V. Raman, 1921, molecular scattering); reflection of the sky adds a little. The printed answer 'interference of reflected sunlight' is wrong.

s: Oceanic logging means
answer: Ocean water spread to nearby lands.
src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
x: The question is loosely worded (likely a translation); the printed meaning – sea water spreading over and waterlogging nearby low land, i.e. coastal inundation – is kept.

s: Which of the following Planetary climatic event is associated with El Nino?
answer: Heat and high rainfall lead to flooding of the coastal zone of South America, especially Peru and Ecuador and also the Pacific coast of Colombia and northern Chile
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: El Nino brings heat and heavy rain to the normally arid coast of Peru and Ecuador (and coastal Colombia, northern Chile), flooding it, while Indonesia and northern Australia get drought.

s: The region above aphotic zone, having insufficient light for photosynthesis, in the ocean is called as
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: The disphotic (twilight) zone lies above the aphotic zone; some light reaches it, but too little for photosynthesis.

s: Which of the following zones has highest percentage of marine habitats?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: The epipelagic (sunlit) zone, the top ~200 m, holds the largest share of marine habitats and life because photosynthesis happens there.

s: In the open sea, the zone extending from the high water to the low water zone of the coastal belt, upto a depth of 200 m inside the sea, is called:
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: The neritic zone runs from the high-water line over the continental shelf to about 200 m depth; it is the richest fishing zone.

s: Which of the following is a real fish?
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: The sea horse (Hippocampus) is a true bony fish (Osteichthyes); sea cow and sea lion are mammals, and starfish, jellyfish and cuttlefish are not fish. Moved to marine organisms (row 26).

s: Meteorological drought means
answer: The degree of dryness or rainfall deficit and the length of the dry period
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: Meteorological drought is defined by rainfall deficiency against the long-period average – the degree of dryness and how long the dry spell lasts – not by soil moisture or reservoir levels.

s: The human factors which cause floods are:
src: APPSC Executive Officer Grade-III in A.P. Endowments Sub-Service Screening Test (Notification 24/2021), Section A (General Studies), held 24-07-2022 · Q39
x: Deforestation increases surface run-off and siltation of rivers, making floods more likely.

s: Strip of trees and shrubs planted for protection of fields from Winds in coastal areas are called
src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test (2018 recruitment), held 28-05-2019 · Q54
x: Shelter belts are rows of trees and shrubs that reduce wind speed and protect crops and soil.

s: Which among the following are the four phases of disaster management planning?
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: The four phases are mitigation, preparation (preparedness), response and recovery.

s: Section ____ of the Disaster Management Act, 2005 empowers Governor of a State to establish State Disaster Management Authority.
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Section 14(1) provides for establishing the SDMA. Strictly the Act says every State Government shall establish it by notification (in the Governor's name).

s: What is the rank of India in the world for natural disasters after China as per UNISDR?
src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
x: UN/UNISDR figures cited in exams put India second after China in natural disasters (e.g. 2010: China 22, India 16).

s: Who first coined the phrase “geographic information system”?
src: APPSC Executive Officer Grade-III in A.P. Endowments Sub-Service Screening Test (Notification 24/2021), Section A (General Studies), held 24-07-2022 · Q36
x: Roger Tomlinson, who built the Canada GIS in the 1960s, coined the term and is called the father of GIS.

s: GIS uses the information from which of the following sources?
src: APPSC Executive Officer Grade-III in A.P. Endowments Sub-Service Screening Test (Notification 24/2021), Section A (General Studies), held 24-07-2022 · Q40
x: A GIS works on spatial (location-referenced) data.

s: The World Fisheries Day is observed on
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: World Fisheries Day is observed on 21 November; National Fish Farmers' Day is 10 July.

s: The National fish farmer's day is observed on
src: APPSC Group-III Mains Panchayat Secretary (Grade-IV) Paper-I
x: National Fish Farmers' Day (10 July) marks the induced breeding of carps on 10 July 1957 by Dr Hiralal Chaudhuri and Dr K.H. Alikunhi; World Fisheries Day is 21 November.

s: 'Blue Economy' is related with:
src: APPSC AEE Electrical Engineering Screening Test General Stud
x: The blue economy is the sustainable use of ocean (marine) resources for growth, livelihoods and ecosystem health.

s: Which of the following country is the largest producer of pearls?
src: APPSC Group-II Services Main Examination (Notification 25/2018), Paper I: General Studies and Mental Ability, held 29-08-2019 (Shift 1; Mental Ability questions omitted) · Q56
x: APPSC keys Japan, historically the leading producer of cultured pearls.

s: Which country is the World's largest producer of solar energy?
src: APPSC Deputy Executive Information Engineers & Inspector of
x: China is the world's largest producer of solar energy (solar power capacity and generation).

s: Who headed the World Commission on Environment and Development?
src: APPSC Executive Officer Grade-III in A.P. Endowments Sub-Service Screening Test (Notification 24/2021), Section A (General Studies), held 24-07-2022 · Q37
x: The WCED (Brundtland Commission), whose 1987 report 'Our Common Future' defined sustainable development, was chaired by Gro Harlem Brundtland.

s: Dakshin Gangotri is _____________?
answer: Indian Scientific Base Station in Antartica
src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test (2018 recruitment), held 28-05-2019 · Q50
x: Dakshin Gangotri, set up in 1983, was India's first scientific base in Antarctica.

s: Dead Sea is called so because
answer: It is devoid of macroscopic aquatic organisms
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: The Dead Sea is so salty (~240‰) that no fish or other macroscopic aquatic life survives; only microbes live in it.

s: The two deepest lakes ____ in the world, occupy basins formed by complexes of grabens
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x: Lake Baikal and Lake Tanganyika, the two deepest lakes, lie in rift (graben) basins.

s: Browne Waterfalls are situated in
src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
x: Browne Falls lie in Fiordland, South Island, New Zealand (Doubtful Sound) – a world-geography fact, not an Indian waterfall.
